answer.main_body: horizontal corridor tube with side collars and windows
answer.evidence: The entire structure is drawn in a pure front elevation (side-scroller/platformer style). Every horizontal feature—the tube top, upper/lower panel divider, window frames, bottom edge, and the side collars/rings—is a perfectly flat horizontal line with no elliptical curvature or visible top surface receding into depth.
The main tube structure clearly displays its upper curved/sloping top roof surface across rows 2–13 (approx. 12 source pixel rows) above the vertical south face (rows 14–28) containing the windows.

answer.main_body: horizontal pressurized corridor tube with side bulkhead rings
answer.evidence: The asset is drawn in pure 2D side-view/platformer elevation. The upper paneling (rows 2-13) consists of flat vertical ribs and panels rather than a foreshortened top surface, and the side bulkhead pillars terminate in 2D rounded dome outlines (rows 3-4) with no visible top elliptical caps.

The upper curved/sloped top surface of the horizontal pressurized tube is clearly visible across rows 2-13 (12 pixel rows tall) with lighter upward-facing lighting and vertical structural ribs, distinctly transitioning to the darker south vertical wall and window band at row 14.
